A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEDI research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and reorganized theoretical material.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments, SVHN/CIFAR clustering, generation and OOD evaluations, and MNIST neuro-symbolic results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports NeSy-only classification and clustering results in Table 6.

M1.justification: GEDI retains its generative, invariance, and prior terms, jointly optimized using SGLD and Adam in Algorithm 1. The revised logit notation and gradient correction do not establish a different method; the implementation descriptions remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use moons, circles, SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and MNIST, retaining clustering, generation, OOD detection, linear evaluation, and addition-based neuro-symbolic tasks. Reframing the MNIST application as symbol grounding does not change its data or task.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds 'No GEDI (NeSy)' alongside the retained standalone-GEDI and GEDI-with-NeSy configurations. This changes membership in that comparison even though NeSy-only training appeared in an existing appendix analysis. Other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported architectures, augmentation, training budgets, sample sizes, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged, including Tables 7–9 and the linear-probe protocol in Table 10. The additional Table 6 results use the retained MNIST evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The MNIST ablation gains test accuracy and NMI for the NeSy-only configuration, extending evidence beyond its existing training-loss curves. The synthetic loss-term ablations, sensitivity analysis, and appendix comparison of NeSy and invariance losses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-run/seed summaries for clustering, FID, and linear evaluation, and median/standard-deviation reporting in Table 6, are retained. The added entries follow the existing reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds NeSy-only accuracy of 0.10 ± 0.00 and NMI of 0.00 ± 0.00 for each of 100, 1000, and 10000 training examples. Previously reported numerical results and experimental result plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 substantially reworks the formal SSL analysis into Lemmas 3, 6, and 9 with expanded proofs in Appendices A–C, including a gamma-scaled Gaussian prior and normalization conditions for CorInfoMax. It revises the GEDI-bound derivation for joint original/augmented observations and corrects the missing gradient subtraction in v2 Equation (15), now Equation (7).

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refocus the neuro-symbolic contribution on a specific symbol-grounding example. The introduction also removes the claim of avoiding additional computational costs relative to purely discriminative approaches. Joint generative/discriminative training and avoidance of the three failure modes remain central claims.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly specifies that the analysis covers purely encoder-based techniques and defers predictive models such as masked autoencoders. Existing qualifications concerning known class counts/priors, larger-scale evaluation, and inconsistent OOD performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture and hyperparameter disclosures, MNIST addition-data construction, code-source attribution, and the promised code release upon acceptance are retained after appendix matching. The new NeSy diagram and expanded probability notation explain the existing setup without disclosing a different implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Harnad (1990) to support the symbol-grounding positioning. It removes the introduction's explicit description of the paper as an integral version of Sansone (2023) extending Sansone and Manhaeve (2022). Most related-work discussion and references remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and Section 2 are substantially rewritten, with a new definition–lemma–explanation structure. Three proof appendices precede the retained appendices, the NeSy exposition is expanded, and funding and author-contribution statements are added.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn and relabelled with color, Figure 1 is relocated, and a NeSy architecture diagram is added as Figure 7. Table 6 gains a comparison group. Existing experimental plots are retained, with appendix figures renumbered and some displays relocated.

improvement.justification: The added MNIST control, more explicit assumptions, and correction of the generative-gradient subtraction improve assessability. However, the expanded proofs introduce internal inconsistencies: v3 Appendix A Equation (13) subtracts KL while asserting the opposite inequality, and Appendix B reverses the log-determinant sign during simplification. These defects weaken the new theoretical support, leaving the net effect of the explanatory gains and mathematical regressions unclear.
